_comment: Layout constants that are not expressible inside the Anchor IDL. Account lengths are byte-exact and double as getProgramAccounts dataSize filters, so a drift here is a silent empty scan — test/idl.test.mjs re-derives every length from the IDL type definitions and fails if this file disagrees.

reserveWidths._comment: The launch reserve: zero bytes appended pre-deploy that future fields are carved from, front-first, so accountLens never move. Deployer has had 26 bytes carved (btc_share_bps u16 + epoch_units_bought u64 + btc_units_bought u64 + user_flags u64).

flags._comment: Bit INDICES into WkConfig.flags (u64). The flag value is 1n << index.

userFlags._comment: Bit INDICES into Deployer.user_flags (u64) — the switches a USER owns, moved only by set_user_flags(mask, value) signed by the manager authority. An operator can never write them. The value is 1n << index, and 0 is always the pre-existing behaviour, which is why the field could be carved into live accounts without a migration. PAUSE_MINING stops deploys only: settles, claims, prize collection and withdrawals all keep running. HOLD_VAULT_BUYS stops BOTH ticket legs so hashrate banks on the Miner; it does not stop claim_sats, which is money owed to the user. HOLD_SATS stops claim_sats so the position keeps its SatsVault shares and earns the 10% fee every OTHER claimer pays; the cost is that claim_sats is the only thing that releases locked hashrate, so holding freezes 35% of everything mined, and it is enforced ONLY when the caller passes the Deployer as a fifth remaining account (see remainingAccounts) — a four-account caller claims for a holder as before. A mask touching any bit not listed here is rejected with BadSetting.

remainingAccounts._comment: Per-user remaining_accounts, in order, for the batch instructions whose shape the IDL cannot express — an IDL describes named accounts, and these are a repeating run appended after them. Transcribed from the program source (claim.rs) and verified against the deployed program by simulation, NOT inferred. Only wk_claim_sats_batch is published here because only its shape has been proven both ways; the other batch instructions have a single fixed stride and are not yet published rather than being guessed at.

wk_claim_sats_batch._comment: FOUR or FIVE accounts per user, and the choice is the caller's. Four is what every client deployed before 2026-08-20 sends and it still works exactly as it did — the upgrade could not require five without failing every live caller from the moment it landed. Five adds the position's Deployer, which is the account carrying user_flags, and is what lets the program see HOLD_SATS at all: a four-account call cannot read the flag so it claims for a holder regardless. Any other multiple is refused with BadRemainingAccounts (6021). Passing another position's Deployer is refused with BadPda (6003), so a caller cannot choose which switch to read. The signer matters: when the signer IS the position's own authority the hold is ignored and the claim proceeds — that is the force-sweep, and it needs no separate instruction.

seeds._comment: PDA seed recipes, in order. kind=literal is UTF-8 bytes of value; kind=pubkey is the named account's 32 bytes; u16le/u32le/u64le are the named argument little-endian.

satrush._comment: Sat Rush is a third-party program WhiteKnight CPIs into. Sizes were verified against live mainnet accounts of every type; its upgrade authority can redeploy at any time, so clients must length-check before decoding and halt on mismatch rather than read shifted fields.
